cups_proxy: start when starting concierge Cups proxy does not need concierge services, so we do not need to wait for it to start. In fact, we want it to be already started when concierge runs, because we expect all services that concierge/VMs depend on to be started so that concierge can service requests as soon as it is running. pytest: Add daemon to check device rotation during stylus test Currently the stylus test doesn't support receiving stylus events in different orientations, but the screen is still rotatable during test. Thus the path on canvas may be rotated to another undesired orientation, and results in test failures though we draw the line in "correct" way. This CL adds a daemon thread to monitor the rotation, warn on the wrong direction and only allow test started in correct way. iproute2: Resync ARL qdisc attributes The ARL qdisc defines several Netlink attributes that are 64bit quantities. With the introduction of the nla_put_u64_64bit() helper [commit 73520786b079 ("libnl: add nla_put_u64_64bit() helper")] these attributes are forced to 64bit alignment. A new ARL attribute (TCA_ARL_PAD) is defined in the kernel pkt_sched.h file, which is inserted in the Netlink message when padding is required to achieve the necessary 64bit attribute alignment. The iproute2 package maintains its own private copy of the kernel pkt_sched.h file. This CL synchronizes the kernel TCA_ARL_xxx attribute list with the iproute2 private pkt_sched.h, this picks up the new TCA_ARL_PAD to ensure the 'tc qdisc show' command can properly recognize and decode Netlink messages when ARL Qdisc is active. BUG=b:138685581 TEST=System test: % tc qdisc add dev wan0 root handle 1: arl minrate 4800kbit \ buffer 5000 limit 500 latency 100ms latency_hysteresis 30ms % tc -s qdisc show dev wan0 Change-Id: I81aaedb904b4b8afffd879380faad72e60600ab3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1732488 Tested-by: Danny Mitzel <mitzel@google.com> Commit-Ready: Danny Mitzel <mitzel@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>
